clue.text: Like this clue, within potential bidder's range

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other, here the clue's direction inside the bridge player

parts.note: in bridge, South is one of the four players who bid; the possessive 's supplies the final S
this is a Down clue, so it is like a down

explanation.surface: Someone describes a clue as lying within the reach of a would-be bidder at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The SOUTH DOWNS are a range of chalk hills in southern England. The clue refers to itself: it is printed among the Down clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The named hills form a chalk range running across Sussex and Hampshire.

clue.text: Those with a short time to live make the border in record time

definitions.text: Those with a short time to live

indicators.note: in places the edging piece inside the record-and-time pair

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: Short-lived creatures manage to make a border in record-breaking time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things, such as mayflies, that last only a day or so.

clue.text: Does business from extra desktop

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone does business with a spare computer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to buy and sell, so trades is a synonym for does business.

clue.text: Buy a rusty Datsun estate, initially repaired for a song

indicators.note: repaired suggests something put back together differently, so these letters are rearranged
initially picks the opening letters of the two car words

explanation.surface: Advice to purchase an old rusty Datsun estate car, fixed up, for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' reads as the idiom 'very cheaply', but 'a song' is the definition, with 'for' linking it. The rearranged pool is BUY, A, RUSTY plus D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The named track is a well-known Rolling Stones single, so it is an example of a song.

clue.text: Started touring after struggling to entertain very much

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the word for started encloses the other piece

parts.note: begun means started

indicators.note: struggling suggests something in disarray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tour began after a struggle to keep the audience amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Started touring' reads as setting off on a tour, but 'touring' is the signal that one piece goes round another, and 'struggling' shuffles the word after.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is highly enjoyable entertains a great deal, so the phrase matches the idiom.

clue.text: Very thin ogress desperately eating a piece of meat

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other, so the shuffled monster encloses the rest
desperately suggests wild disorder, so the monster's letters are rearranged
piece of takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A frantic ogress devours a chunk of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' turns OGRESS into GOSSER, and 'eating' puts A and M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer describes something as fine and delicate as cobweb thread.

clue.text: Material lawyer has to cover

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
a mask covers the face

explanation.surface: A lawyer is asked to cover some material.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: The majority of 20 so different to 11?

parts.note: the answer at 20 is a weekday whose usual one-letter abbreviation is M

indicators.note: different means the two-letter word is rearranged

parts.note: the answer at 11 is a weekday abbreviated as T

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how most of one entry differs from another.
explanation.walkthrough: '20 ... to 11' reads like a shop's opening days, M to T, with OS (from 'so', made 'different') between.
explanation.definitionFit: Most and the majority of both mean more than half of something.

clue.text: Timely work on river — River Aire, say

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
R is the map abbreviation for river
the Yorkshire river Aire sounds like air, which is a tune

explanation.surface: A timely piece of work about a river, perhaps the Aire in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Aire' looks like one name, but it splits into R and a sound-alike: Aire said aloud gives air, a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means coming at a convenient or well-chosen time, which is timely.

clue.text: Share of quota good enough for distant region

indicators.note: Share of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A good enough share of the quota is allotted to a far-off area.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'enough for distant region' as the definition, but 'enough' does not define a region: 'distant region' alone is the definition and 'enough for' links. OTAGO is a region of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island, about as far from Britain as one can go.

clue.text: See 4
Jack in support boot again?

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the word for support

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or an arm
a jack tar, or simply jack or tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A jack fitted into a support, ready to boot someone once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' is the computing sense: to start a machine up.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart a computer is to boot it up a second time.

clue.text: Vehicles for two players get ordered a year from 11

indicators.note: ordered means the remaining letters are put into a new sequence
from means the named letters are taken away from the weekday

parts.note: the answer at 11 is a weekday
a gives A and Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Two musicians are told to take a year off from a weekday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes A and Y out of TUESDAY, leaving TUESD, which 'ordered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece written for two performers, a vehicle for their playing.

clue.text: See 16
Aged count unhappy about one sharp talker?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the numeral piece
unhappy suggests something out of sorts, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly nobleman in a bad mood seems to have a cutting manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' rearranges AGED COUNT, and 'about' puts I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an acid tongue is caustic in speech, a sharp talker in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Putting eg Brown Sugar on top of singles making No 1 around 10

indicators.note: top of, in a down clue, takes the first letter of the word that follows
around means the urinating word encloses the number

parts.note: No 1 is a childish euphemism for urinating, so making one is weeing
ten written as a word

explanation.surface: A record executive sweetens up a Rolling Stones single to make it a chart topper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown Sugar' looks like the Rolling Stones song among 'singles' and 'No 1', but here it is just sugar. 'No 1' is a nursery word for a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding sugar to food or drink is sweetening it.

clue.text: A song and a dance defy karma, as the wife found out

indicators.note: found out suggests the truth worked out in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.words: a dance defy karma, as the wife

explanation.surface: A man's song and dance, defying fate, ends when his wife discovers what he has been up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a song and a dance' looks like a fuss, but 'A song' is the definition and 'and' links it. The fodder is every word from 'a dance' to 'wife'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the title of a famous standard, sung by Dinah Washington among others, so it is a song.

clue.text: Unwanted bubbles hospital removed from two cases of shock

indicators.note: removed from says the hospital letter is taken out of the first word

parts.note: a shock of hair: hair is one example of a shock
H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs
locks are the second example, since a shock is a mass of locks

explanation.surface: Bubbles that nobody wants force a hospital to discharge two patients suffering shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two cases of shock' gives two words that each mean a shock of hair: HAIR (losing H) and LOCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlocks are trapped bubbles of air that block the flow in a pipe.

clue.text: Dark atmosphere from tune at the end of the day

definitions.meaning: the air outdoors after nightfall, when it is dark

definitions.text: tune at the end of the day
definitions.meaning: a tune or air played at night, the end of the day

explanation.definitionFit: The evening air is the atmosphere after dark, and an air sung at night is a night tune.

clue.text: Mum to girl in hospital: "I'm no paid help"

indicators.note: in places the mother and girl inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ma is a word for mum
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A mother speaks to her daughter in hospital, insisting she is a volunteer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a speech: a Samaritan is a volunteer, so helps without pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A good Samaritan helps strangers freely, and the charity's volunteers are unpaid listeners.

clue.text: See 23 and 24
TGIF back without first sign of hiccuping bout

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the reversed letters surround the next piece
back means the four letters are read in the opposite direction
first sign of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: After a Friday night out someone has a bout of hiccups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TGIF into FIGT, and 'without' puts it around H. 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a bout, as in a boxing contest.

clue.text: TGI … an unusually fair, dry vacation?

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are rearranged out of their normal order
vacation empties the word, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A holiday that turns out unusually fair and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but empties DRY to DY, which joins FAIR in the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: TGI stands for 'thank God it's', the slogan completed by the last working day of the week.

clue.text: 21 across over this, perhaps

definitions.meaning: twenty-one, the card game also called vingt-et-un
a floating bridge is something one goes across over

explanation.walkthrough: '21 across' looks like a reference to another clue, but '21' is the card game and 'across over this' the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon is the British name for the card game twenty-one and also a floating bridge.

clue.text: Bar placed on English one in hairy group

indicators.note: placed on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: A bar is put on top of an English one in a shaggy band.
explanation.definitionFit: A pube is slang for a single pubic hair, one of a hairy group.

clue.text: Composer of a type of pop number

parts.note: Britpop is a type of pop music
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A songwriter of a certain kind of pop number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop number' reads as a song, but 'number' is TEN. Benjamin BRITTEN was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was an English composer of operas such as Peter Grimes.

clue.text: Buy me an old-fashioned number

indicators.note: fashioned means made into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for someone to buy a cocktail, an Old Fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like the cocktail or an adjective on 'number', but the hyphen splits it: 'old' is fodder and 'fashioned' the signal. The answer is a New Order single.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song, and the answer is a well-known New Order single.

clue.text: Moby Dick anal? Not the current version, one dated 19/10/87

indicators.note: Not says the letter for current must be left out of the pool
version means a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A critic sniffs that a pedantic new edition of Moby Dick is not up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: MOBY DICK ANAL without I, the physics symbol for current, is rearranged by 'version'. The answer names the stock market crash of 19 October 1987.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the name given to the day of the 1987 stock market crash.

clue.text: Return No 1, thanks to Scottish singer wailing

indicators.note: Return means the whole string is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for 1
ta is a British informal thanks
Lulu is a Scottish pop singer

explanation.surface: A Scottish singer is asked to bring back her number one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reverses the whole string NOITALULU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ululation is a long wavering howl of grief, a kind of wailing.
